clue.text: Bird in net's in Burns country?

definitions.note: the poet Robert Burns came from the Scottish southern lowland region; the question mark flags a definition by example

indicators.note: the bird is placed inside the other piece, as 'in' says here

parts.note: to net a fish is to land it, so 'net's' (nets) gives lands
the owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird caught in a net somewhere in Robert Burns's Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' is the Scottish poet Robert Burns, not a stream (burn) or a fire; his home ground was the south of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns was born and lived in Ayrshire, part of the low-lying southern region of Scotland.

clue.text: Part of mouth used by chap who was seen making a famous phone call

definitions.text: who was seen making a famous phone call

parts.note: the lip is part of the mouth
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a man's lips on a well-known phone advert.
explanation.walkthrough: Maureen Lipman played Beattie in a long-running British Telecom TV advertising campaign of phone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress is famous in Britain for her BT advertisements as a grandmother on the telephone.

clue.text: One is in a confused state with carriage on roundabout

parts.note: to be in a whirl is to be confused
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gig is a light two-wheeled carriage

explanation.surface: A muddled passenger in a carriage on a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' is a fairground merry-go-round, not a road junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling toy or merry-go-round is something that spins round and round.

clue.text: Archer's fictional pal once needing to take care with targets

definitions.meaning: in Farquhar's play The Beaux' Stratagem, Archer's friend is a fortune-hunting gentleman
to point accurately at what you mean to hit

explanation.surface: An archer's old friend is told to aim carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: Archer is a character name, not a bowman, in George Farquhar's 1707 comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Farquhar named the two adventurers in his comedy Archer and his companion, who must point carefully at targets.

clue.text: English poet's play with music, not once rejected in a kind way

parts.note: to do a play is to stage it, so 'play' gives do
rag is ragtime music

indicators.note: the 'never' word is turned back to front, as being rejected suggests

parts.note: ne'er, never, means not once
well can mean kindly, as in 'treat someone well'

explanation.surface: An English poet's musical drama is turned down nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns NE'ER into REEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dora Greenwell was a Victorian poet from County Durham who wrote religious verse.

clue.text: Performs badly in parts of drama at Cambridge

parts.note: a play is divided into acts
being 'up' means being in residence at a university such as Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone gives a poor performance in a student play at Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Being UP at a university (especially Oxford or Cambridge) is British usage for being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to behave or function badly, as a misbehaving child or a faulty machine does.

clue.text: European conspirator about to fool one American

parts.note: C is circa, about
an ass is a fool
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A European plotter is about to make a fool of an American.
explanation.definitionFit: He was one of the Roman senators who plotted against Julius Caesar.

clue.text: "It's neutral" was not quite right about Switzerland

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase standing for a noun

indicators.note: the reworked letters go round the Swiss code, as 'about' suggests
being not right means put wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Someone insists a neutral country was misrepresented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite right' rearranges WAS into SWA, which goes round CH. 'neutral' looks like a nod to Swiss neutrality.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics this is the neutral, unstressed vowel sound heard in the first syllable of 'about'.

clue.text: Tools fasten nuts

parts.note: to pin is to fasten
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: Instructions for fixing nuts with tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tools' is slang for idiots, not implements; 'nuts' are heads, not hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for stupid people, fools.

clue.text: Greek king's boat or other vehicle carrying one from Rome

indicators.note: one piece carries the other inside it, so 'carrying' signals a container

parts.note: a pram is a flat-bottomed dinghy as well as a baby carriage
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Greek monarch owns a boat or carriage holding a Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: PRAM is both a small boat and a baby carriage, which is why the clue gives both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Iliad the ruler of Troy is a king of the Greek-myth world, father of Hector and Paris.

clue.text: Jolt when reversing on one way to Chinese part of Asia

indicators.note: the jolt word is read backwards, as 'reversing' tells us

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or jarring shock
A is one, as in 'a book'
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
the Han are China's majority ethnic group

explanation.surface: A bumpy reverse manoeuvre on a road leading into China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns JAR into RAJ.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large desert state in north-west India, so a region within that continent.

clue.text: Co-authored stories that are created with Banks?

definitions.meaning: tales written by two people together
bank accounts opened by two people in partnership

explanation.surface: Stories written in collaboration with the novelist Banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like the novelist Iain Banks, but means financial banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Two writers' shared narratives are joint tales, and shared bank holdings are opened jointly.

clue.text: Herb's working with gal — an illustrator called Janet

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new order, signalling a rearrangement here

parts.note: the 's is the clue's 'is' and adds no letter

explanation.surface: A man named Herb and a girl team up with an artist called Janet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges HERB and GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Janet and Allan Ahlberg made famous children's picture books, she drawing the pictures he wrote words for.

clue.text: Do what's current, in Jessica's statement in a soap opera

indicators.note: the current symbol goes inside the statement, as 'in' says

parts.words: Jessica's statement in a soap opera
parts.note: Jessica Tate, a character in the US sitcom Soap, might introduce herself as 'I'm Tate'
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Copying the fashion by quoting a soap character's line.
explanation.walkthrough: Jessica Tate is a lead character in the American comedy series Soap, a parody of soap operas.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is to mimic them, as a comedian does an impression of a politician.

clue.text: British lyricist meets an American singer, an egoist encountered in Florence

parts.note: W S Gilbert wrote the words for Gilbert and Sullivan's operettas
Donny Osmond is an American pop singer

explanation.surface: An English operetta writer bumps into a US pop star and a vain man in Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: The egoist is the selfish husband in Henry James's The Portrait of a Lady, whom Isabel Archer meets in Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James's novel depicts this aesthete as a cold, self-absorbed man living near Florence.

clue.text: Early Shakespeare character called John Peel?

definitions.meaning: Sir John was Shakespeare's first name for the fat knight later renamed Falstaff
a peel is an old fortified tower in the Scottish borders, so a John who is a peel

explanation.surface: An early Shakespeare figure took the name of the radio DJ John Peel.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel suggests the British radio DJ or the huntsman of the song, but a peel is a small border fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff was first named after the Lollard knight Sir John, and a peel tower is an ancient fortification.

clue.text: Sue's confused about cryptic clue for an empire founder

indicators.note: one jumbled set wraps around the other, as 'about' signals
being confused jumbles these letters into a new order

parts.note: here the 's supplies a letter, giving sues

indicators.note: a cryptic word is mysterious, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Sue is puzzled by a cryptic clue about the founder of an empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes SEUS from SUES and 'cryptic' makes LEUC from CLUE; SEUS goes 'about' LEUC.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great's general founded the dynasty that ruled a vast Asian empire after Alexander's death.

clue.text: Oxford literary institution's crooked aid challenged

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest grant to an Oxford institution is disputed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges AID and CHALLENGED.
explanation.definitionFit: This Oxford pub is where Tolkien, C S Lewis and the Inklings met to discuss their writing.

clue.text: Comic actor Arthur's nationality

definitions.meaning: Arthur ... was a British comedian, known from Are You Being Served?
the national identity of people from England

explanation.surface: Asking where a comic actor called Arthur comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur English played Mr Harman in the sitcom Are You Being Served?, and people born in England have this nationality.

clue.text: Fellow in a foreign country, in a Poe poem

indicators.note: the fellow abbreviation sits inside the country, as 'in' says

parts.note: Israel is a country abroad

explanation.surface: A man abroad appears in a poem by Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe's 1831 lyric is named after the angel of music in Islamic tradition.

clue.text: Mythical sisters having year in Hell

indicators.note: the year letter is put inside the underworld, as 'in' signals

parts.note: Hades is the underworld, hell

explanation.surface: Legendary sisters spend a year in the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these nymphs, daughters of Atlas, were placed in the sky as a star cluster.

clue.text: Typically conversational poem about a translator of classical verse on Europe

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the following pieces after the Europe letter

parts.note: C stands for circa, about
Christopher Logue reworked Homer's Iliad in his War Music

explanation.surface: A Homer translator writes a chatty poem on a European theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's pastoral poems of this kind are often dialogues between shepherds.

clue.text: Discover a poet with a touch of naturalism

parts.note: Edward Lear was a nonsense poet

indicators.note: a touch is a tiny bit, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Finding a poet with a slight naturalist leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out a fact is to discover it.

clue.text: She's usually seen in blue in a Coleridge poem

definitions.text: She's usually seen in blue in a Coleridge poem

parts.words: She's usually seen in blue in a Coleridge poem
parts.note: the Virgin Mary is traditionally painted in a blue robe, and Coleridge's verse invokes Mary, mother of Christ

explanation.surface: A woman in blue features in a poem by Coleridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Religious painting dresses Mary in blue; Coleridge's poems such as Christabel call on her by name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the reverent title Catholics give to Mary, mother of Jesus.

clue.text: Talk in a bad way about an ambassador to England

parts.note: to chat is to talk
ill means unwell, in a bad way
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Sick talk regarding a diplomat sent to England.
explanation.walkthrough: The ambassador is the French envoy in Shakespeare's King John.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's King John this character is the French king's envoy who brings the challenge to the English court.

clue.text: Cursed Lawrence in a rage

indicators.note: Lawrence's initials go inside the craze word, as 'in' indicates

parts.note: a fad is a craze, 'all the rage'
T E Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Lawrence furiously swearing in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rage' is a craze here, not anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doomed by destiny is ill-starred, as if under a curse.

clue.text: Companion to European Saint Oscar, or in part, companion to a knight

parts.note: San is saint in Spanish and Italian
CH stands for Companion of Honour
Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: A list of honours mixing a saint, an Oscar and a knight's sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight is Don Quixote, and his squire is Sancho Panza.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes gives Don Quixote a squire who rides beside him on a donkey.

clue.text: Writer's final thoughts about change in Bible excerpts

parts.note: a PS, postscript, is what a letter writer adds at the end
to alter is to change, so 'change' as a verb gives alters

explanation.surface: An author's afterthoughts concern a change to a Bible passage.
explanation.definitionFit: These are books holding the psalms, a part of Scripture, often printed separately for worship.
